title: The Endomembrane System
short: A protein made for export follows a path: ribosomes on the rough ER, then a vesicle to the Golgi apparatus, then a vesicle to the cell membrane, where it is released.
trouble: Students send proteins from the nucleus straight to the Golgi, or think the Golgi makes proteins. Ribosomes make them; the ER and Golgi fold, tag and ship them.

blocks.html: Some cells make proteins to send out: digestive enzymes from the pancreas, mucus from the lining of the nose, antibodies from white blood cells. Those proteins follow one route through the cell, a connected set of membranes called the endomembrane system.

A protein made for export follows a path: ribosomes on the rough ER build it into the ER, a vesicle carries it to the Golgi apparatus, the Golgi modifies and sorts it, and another vesicle carries it to the cell membrane, where it is released.

blocks.name: bi-feedback

steps: A ribosome on the rough ER builds the protein, threading it into the ER
The ER folds the protein; a transport vesicle buds off
The Golgi apparatus modifies, tags and sorts it
A secretory vesicle carries it to the cell membrane
The vesicle fuses with the membrane and the protein is released (exocytosis)
opts.title: The path of a protein made for export

blocks.cap: Five steps, always in this order.

blocks.name: bi-cell
blocks.cap: Find the parts of the path: nucleus (where the instructions are), rough ER, Golgi apparatus and cell membrane.

blocks.html: The instructions start in the nucleus as DNA; a copy (mRNA) leaves through pores in the nuclear envelope. The ribosomes do the building. Ribosomes floating free in the cytoplasm make proteins that stay in the cytoplasm. Ribosomes stuck to the rough ER (that is what makes it "rough") feed their protein straight into the ER, which folds it. The Golgi works like a post office: it adds tags such as sugar chains and sends each protein to the right place. The smooth ER, with no ribosomes, makes lipids instead. Lysosomes are made by the same path: they are vesicles of digestive enzymes from the Golgi.

blocks.title: Follow the label
blocks.q: In the early 1960s, George Palade's lab gave pancreas cells radioactive amino acids for a few minutes, then followed where the label went. In what order would it appear?
steps: Amino acids are built into proteins at the ribosomes on the rough ER, so the label shows up there first.
Next it moves in vesicles to the Golgi.
Then it appears in secretory vesicles near the cell membrane, and finally outside the cell.
blocks.a: Rough ER, Golgi, secretory vesicles, outside the cell

blocks.html: Sending proteins from the nucleus straight to the Golgi, or saying the Golgi makes proteins. The nucleus holds the instructions; ribosomes make the proteins; the ER and Golgi fold, tag and ship them. Check your path: it always passes through the ER before the Golgi, and vesicles carry the protein between each stop.
